drivers.variant_notes: Production 1980 machine with four six-digit player displays; GEN_BY35, SNDBRD_BY51 and no auxiliary lamp columns.
Oliver seven-digit conversion firmware (2004), same playfield I/O, requires seven-digit player-display hardware; not another manufactured physical edition. Numeric coil-test routing matches original.

mechanisms.behavior: Four serially exposed targets A (top/rear), B, C, D (bottom/front). Ball first reaches D; each fallen target closes its own contact and stays down until public 1 resets the common bank. Exposes standup 5. Reset at game/ball start; keep held contacts down until reset, then release them.
mechanisms.label: Four-target inline bank

mechanisms.behavior: Targets 1 (top), 2, 3 (bottom) have separate switches 19, 18, 17. Public 2 resets all three; public 3/4/5 trip their respective target latch down, which must close 19/18/17. Switch 33 is a separate rebound behind the bank. Completing the bank resets it; 1-2-3 order gives 10x lit value. The retained table omits all three individual trip callbacks and rebound 33.
mechanisms.label: Three-target bank with individual trip coils

mechanisms.behavior: One cup and occupancy switch 32, two opposite kickers. Unlit entry fires 9 down toward left bumper; after A/B collect-bonus qualification it fires 8 up toward rear arch. Both paths must clear 32 when the ball actually leaves; modeled sensor writes are ball-state inputs.
mechanisms.label: Bidirectional upper-left saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Occupancy 24 requests public 17, ejecting forward through the spinner toward left flipper. Close while ball rests and release on exit; retain ball until successful ejection.
mechanisms.label: Top-center saucer

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests on 8 at initial setup. Coin/start enables relay 19, resets banks and fires 7 to send ball to manual shooter lane. Hold 8 until physical ball leaves; subsequent drain starts bonus/ball progression. VPX BallRelease shooter kicker is a routing helper; physical outhole is Drain.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball drain and serve

mechanisms.behavior: Ball closes its leaf contact; ROM pulses the matching coil. Bumper rod/skirt or sling rubber supplies mechanical motion; leave speed and animation tuning table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: K1 relay 19 powers hard-wired cabinet buttons and dual-wound flippers. Buttons 82/84 are the host inputs; 46/48 are synthetic effect callbacks, 45/47 duplicate runtime states. Physical EOS switches handle winding changes locally and are not modeled as game-matrix sensors.
mechanisms.label: Two relay-enabled flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Each spinner revolution pulses 14; passive gate admits ball. Starts at 10 points, pays 100 after 10 spins and 1000 after 20 spins; warning sound announces reset, a new spin retains current tier. No actuator.
mechanisms.label: Passive spinner and gate

mechanisms.behavior: Public 6 pulses cabinet knocker AR-26-1200 against its strike surface. No feedback sensor; the numeric service test identifies printed 02.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet knocker

mechanisms.behavior: Coin-door coil FO-36-7000 is continuous public 18, printed test 16. Preserve controller state; it is not a playfield kicker and has no game-matrix feedback sensor.
mechanisms.label: Coin-door lockout assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Passive ball gate at the left side of the rear arch. No CPU actuator or matrix sensor; keep one-way ball passage consistent with the factory playfield drawing.
mechanisms.label: Left upper-arch gate

mechanisms.behavior: Passive ball gate at the right side of the rear arch. No CPU actuator or matrix sensor; stop angle and friction are table tuning.
mechanisms.label: Right upper-arch gate

mechanisms.behavior: Two passive gate-and-wire assemblies in the left/right flipper-feed lanes, as counted by the factory parts table. No CPU output; preserve their one-way ball passage.
mechanisms.label: Two flipper-feed ball gates
